sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Security headers, redirects and build tweak
sections.what: Sends strict security headers on every page, redirects three old dashboard paths to the profile page, and stops disk caching in production builds.
sections.why: The comments say the headers are for a healthcare app and the cache change prevents disk-full errors.
sections.watch_out: The strict transport header with preload is hard to reverse. Test it on a staging address before relying on it.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Analyzer and error tracking wrapper
sections.what: Wraps the settings so bundle size can be inspected when ANALYZE is set, and so errors are reported to Sentry with source maps kept private.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the team see large bundles and get readable error reports without exposing source code. The comments support this.
sections.watch_out: Readable error traces only work if the Sentry organization and project names are right. The silent setting hides upload failures.

summary: Build and runtime settings for the web app: security headers, old-path redirects, a build tweak, and wrappers for bundle size and error tracking.
purpose: Controls how the web app is built and what headers browsers receive.
why: The header comment says it is a healthcare app, which explains the strict security headers. Other reasons not stated in the code.
how: Adds security headers to every page, redirects three old dashboard paths to the profile page, turns off disk caching in production builds, and wraps the settings with the bundle analyzer and Sentry.
inputs: Environment settings ANALYZE, SENTRY_ORG and SENTRY_PROJECT.
outputs: The build settings Next.js uses, and headers sent with each page.
risks: The strict transport header includes preload, which is hard to undo once browsers have accepted it. The sentry key inside the Next settings may not be read by Next.js, so it may do nothing.
debug: If pages are blocked from framing or HTTPS behaviour is odd, check the headers. If builds are slow or disk-heavy, check the cache setting. If error reports lack readable traces, check the Sentry names.
